newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE sets record close on Wall St strength.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE sets record close on Wall St strength.

text.p: The UK stock market climbed to a record close on Monday, buoyed by bid speculation and a further rise on Wall Street.

The FTSE 100 index of leading shares ended at 4,073.1 points, up 20 points on the day and just a fraction off the new all-time high of 4,073.2 points set in late afternoon trading as Wall Street reversed early losses to climb to record heights.

Traders cautioned that the FTSE 100 index had spent much of the quiet session trapped in a narrow range and had simply hitched a lift upwards with the U.S. market amid a lack of major UK corporate news or data.

"The Dow is looking very good indeed but if hadn't been for the U.S. we wouldn't have got up here. The UK is really leaning on someone else for direction and you have to wonder what would happen if that crutch was taken away," one dealer said.

Traders noted that the FTSE's gains came chiefly from bid talk around media group Pearson and pharmaceuticals group Zeneca, gains in oil stocks, retailers and heavyweights British Aerospace and Glaxo.
The record run masked the fact some 33 of the FTSE's 100 stocks ended lower, with seven shares unchanged, while the FTSE 250 mid-capitalisation index shed 0.7 point to 4,449.4 points.
